sessions.first_user_prompt:
Write a COBOL program (GnuCOBOL) for the "Game of 15".

Rules: Two players alternate picking a number from {1, 2, ..., 9}. A number cannot be picked twice. A player wins when any three of their chosen numbers sum to exactly 15. If all nine numbers are picked and no player has won, the game is a draw.

The program should enumerate every possible game (every legal sequence of moves to completion) and report:

Player 1 wins (player who picks first)
Player 2 wins
Draws
Total games

spec_backlog.title: **Iterative DFS with explicit stack**. Single `PERFORM UNTIL DONE=1` driven by `SEARCH-DEPTH` counter + `NEXT-CANDIDATE(depth)` array. Chosen explicitly "to avoid relying on compiler-specific recursion behavior" `[T:event_022]`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **Ownership model + move history + per-depth next-candidate**. `OWNER(9)` holds 0/1/2, `MOVE-NUMBER(9)` records chosen moves, `NEXT-CANDIDATE(9)` holds the next value to try per depth.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **Pre-tabulated player schedule**. `PLAYER-AT-DEPTH(1..9)` explicitly set to `1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2,1` rather than derived modulo.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **Hard-coded tic-tac-toe lines, not magic triples**. Win check is 8 triples but expressed as direct cell triples `{1,5,9},{1,6,8},{2,4,9},{2,5,8},{2,6,7},{3,4,8},{3,5,7},{4,5,6}`, one `IF` per triple. (These are the 8 tic-tac-toe lines *after* the magic-square mapping is applied, so equivalent to the magic-triple set.)
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **Stop-on-win termination rule**. Once `HAS-WON = 1` the branch is recorded and the chosen number is un-owned, rather than completing the remaining picks. Makes the reported total 255,168.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **Formatted reporting with `PIC Z,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZZ,ZZ9`**. Group-separated numeric edit for the three win/draw/total lines.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 1 — Game counter `game15.cob` (commit `29cbcaa`)

spec_backlog.title: **CLI flag parsing via INSPECT TALLYING**. Reads `COMMAND-LINE-TEXT`, wraps with sentinel spaces, counts occurrences of literal `" --unique "` to set `UNIQUE-MODE`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2a — Symmetry deduplication (same commit `c41b9b5`, first sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **D4 symmetry table as number permutations (8 x 9)**. Eight rows of `SYMMETRY-VALUE(sym, n)` mapping number `n` under each square symmetry, stored via individual `MOVE` statements (no REDEFINES / no string literal).
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2a — Symmetry deduplication (same commit `c41b9b5`, first sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Canonical sequence via min-over-orbit**. Keeps a `BEST-MOVE(9)` array; iterates 7 non-identity symmetries, remaps the move list into `TEST-MOVE`, compares lexicographically, swaps in `TEST-MOVE` whenever it is smaller.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2a — Symmetry deduplication (same commit `c41b9b5`, first sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Factorial-rank canonical hash → 986,409-entry bitmap**. Each canonical sequence of length `L` is ranked to an integer in `[0, 9!)` using falling-factorial weights and `LENGTH-OFFSET(L)` start-indices. A `SEEN-CANONICAL PIC X OCCURS 986409` array marks already-counted equivalence classes (`"Y"` or SPACE).
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2a — Symmetry deduplication (same commit `c41b9b5`, first sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Dual counter system**. Four additional `UNIQUE-*` counters incremented only when the canonical sequence is seen for the first time. Always computed; the unique section of the report is gated by `UNIQUE-MODE`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2a — Symmetry deduplication (same commit `c41b9b5`, first sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Base-3 state encoding over all 19,683 boards**. Each of the 3^9 `OWNER`-triplets is mapped to a unique integer `STATE-ID ∈ [1, 19683]` using `POWER3(1..9) = 1,3,9,…,6561`. `STATE-VALID(19683)` and `STATE-OUTCOME(19683)` are full tables, not a transposition cache.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Bottom-up retrograde analysis**. Outer loop `FILLED-TARGET` from 9 down to 0; for each state at that fill level decides validity + outcome by looking up child states (already solved at depth `filled+1`). Guarantees children are ready before the parent.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **State validity filter**. A board is valid iff piece counts are consistent (`p1 ∈ {p2, p2+1}`), not both players have a winning line, and the player who allegedly just moved is the one who won if a win exists. Used to prune ~70% of the 19683 encodings.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Minimax folded into retrograde solve**. `STORE-STATE-OUTCOME` resolves terminal states directly, else picks best-over-children using `BEST-OUTCOME` with early exit when optimum (`1` for P1, `2` for P2) is reached.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Per-level node stack for iterative tree printing**. Fixed-size (depth 10) stack with `NODE-MOVE / NODE-STATE-ID / NODE-OUTCOME / NODE-CHILD-LIST(depth,9) / NODE-BAD-LIST(depth,9) / NODE-NEXT-CHILD / NODE-LAST`. All tree walking is iterative — no `CALL … RECURSIVE`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Optimal-child filter tied to parent value**. Only children whose `STATE-OUTCOME` equals the parent's `NODE-OUTCOME` are expanded; others are set aside (anticipates SB-20).
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **ASCII connectors assembled into `PIC X(120)` line buffer**. `\
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **`--depth N` option with numeric argument validation**. `UNSTRING … DELIMITED BY ALL SPACE` into 8 token slots; rejects non-numeric, caps at 9; `DISPLAY-ELLIPSIS` emits `...` for pruned sub-trees.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: Bug fix: **`FILLED-TARGET` underflow loop**. First attempt declared the counter `PIC 99` (unsigned); the `UNTIL FILLED-TARGET < 0` condition never fired and the solver hung. Agent self-diagnosed from a stalling run, changed to `PIC S99`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: Bug fix: **OWNER array stale after solver phase**. `BUILD-OUTCOME-TABLE` leaves `OWNER` holding the last decoded board, so the tree-print phase was rendering from a non-empty root. Fix: explicit reset loop at the top of `DISPLAY-OPTIMAL-TREE`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2b — Optimal play tree `game15_tree.cob` (same commit `c41b9b5`, second sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **Move classification into safe vs bad buckets**. Same pass as SB-17: children with value == parent go to `NODE-CHILD-MOVE`, others go to `NODE-BAD-MOVE`. Buckets kept per level on the stack.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2c — Avoid annotations (same commit `c41b9b5`, third sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **`avoid:` line rendered at child-level prefix**. `DISPLAY-AVOID-LINE` builds `avoid: n1, n2, …` at the same prefix depth as the optimal children (`PRINT-LEVEL = ACTIVE-LEVEL + 1`). Emitted before the child branches; skipped when `NODE-BAD-COUNT = 0`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2c — Avoid annotations (same commit `c41b9b5`, third sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: Bug fix: **avoid-line indentation reused a stale prefix depth**. Rendered column was one level too shallow. Fix: compute `PRINT-LEVEL` explicitly for each call; run `BUILD-CHILD-PREFIX` with that fresh value.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 2c — Avoid annotations (same commit `c41b9b5`, third sub-step)

spec_backlog.title: **File duplication then display-only diff** (`cp game15.cob game015.cob; cp game15_tree.cob game015tree.cob`). Explicit agent plan: "the search, symmetry, minimax, and avoid logic will stay byte-for-byte aligned".
spec_backlog.phase: Step 3 — Game of 0.15 variants (commit `f9c2eb1`)

spec_backlog.title: **`MOVE-LABEL(9)` lookup for decimal rendering in the tree variant**. `PIC X(4) OCCURS 9` pre-filled with `"0.01" … "0.09"`. Tree node strings and avoid lines use `MOVE-LABEL(NODE-MOVE(level))` instead of raw digit.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 3 — Game of 0.15 variants (commit `f9c2eb1`)

spec_backlog.title: **Target-sum banner text `"Target sum: 0.15"`** in both variants. Single-line cosmetic additions in `REPORT-RESULTS` (counter) and `DISPLAY-ROOT` (tree).
spec_backlog.phase: Step 3 — Game of 0.15 variants (commit `f9c2eb1`)

spec_backlog.title: **Internal integers preserved**. Owner / symmetry / state-id / minimax logic untouched — 0.15 ≡ 15 by factor-of-100. Both variants use the same 986,409 bitmap and 19,683 state table.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 3 — Game of 0.15 variants (commit `f9c2eb1`)

spec_backlog.title: **Two-argument CLI with strict numeric validation**. `UNSTRING … INTO ARG-TOKEN(1..4)`, extra tokens rejected, per-character digit check, `NUMVAL` conversion.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Runtime winning-triple generation**. Nested `a < b < c, a + b + c = target, c ≤ max-number, c > b`; stores up to 84 triples in `TRIPLE-A/B/C`.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Parameterised DFS over `MAX-NUMBER` and `STORED-TRIPLE-COUNT`**. Engine shape identical to SB-01 but with loop bounds read from data; win check iterates stored triples instead of hard-coded lines.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Auto-default `max-number = target-sum - 3`** (clamped to `[3, 999]`). Agent's stated justification: "values above that cannot appear in any distinct winning triple". `(default, capped at 999)` badge shown when capped.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Enumeration guard `MAX-NUMBER <= 9`**. When larger, triples are still listed but the DFS is skipped with an explanatory message, so the program never hangs on combinatorial blow-up.
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Number-pool line-wrapping display**. `DISPLAY-NUMBER-POOL` wraps the pool at 12 entries per line using `FUNCTION MOD(TABLE-IDX, 12) = 0`. Post-validation addition noted in the session as "actual pool listing".
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

spec_backlog.title: **Usage message + explicit default / cap explanation**. `DISPLAY-USAGE` run when `ARGUMENT-ERROR = 1` (triggered by empty or malformed args).
spec_backlog.phase: Step 4 — Generalised Game of N `gameN.cob` (commit `ce67d51`)

<permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `workspace-write`: The sandbox permits reading files, and editing files in `cwd` and `writable_roots`. Editing files in other directories requires approval. Network access is restricted.
# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
- If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with `require_escalated`. ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

### Banned prefix_rules 
Avoid requesting overly broad prefixes that the user would be ill-advised to approve. For example, do not request ["python3"], ["python", "-"], or other similar prefixes that would allow arbitrary scripting.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule argument for destructive commands like rm.
NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring. 

### Examples
Good examples of prefixes:
- ["npm", "run", "dev"]
- ["gh", "pr", "check"]
- ["cargo", "test"]

Write a COBOL program (GnuCOBOL) for the "Game of 15".

Rules: Two players alternate picking a number from {1, 2, ..., 9}. A number cannot be picked twice. A player wins when any three of their chosen numbers sum to exactly 15. If all nine numbers are picked and no player has won, the game is a draw.

The program should enumerate every possible game (every legal sequence of moves to completion) and report:

Player 1 wins (player who picks first)
Player 2 wins
Draws
Total games
I’m checking the workspace structure first so I can place the COBOL program cleanly, then I’ll implement the full game-tree enumeration and verify the reported counts.
The workspace is effectively empty and not a Git checkout. I’m going to create a standalone GnuCOBOL source file here and then compile or at least sanity-check it against the expected game counts.

Plan for the implementation:

1. Create a single standalone GnuCOBOL program that performs a full depth-first search over legal move sequences.
2. Use arrays to track which numbers are taken, which player owns each chosen number, and backtracking state for each move depth.
3. Stop a branch immediately on the first win, count it for the current player, and count a draw only when all nine numbers are consumed without a win.
4. Compile and run it locally to verify the final totals before I hand it over.
I’ve settled on an explicit backtracking implementation rather than recursive self-calls. That keeps the GnuCOBOL source portable and makes the stop-on-first-win rule unambiguous.

I’m writing the standalone COBOL source now. The program uses explicit state tables and backtracking so it can enumerate every legal completed game without relying on compiler-specific recursion behavior.
The source file is in place. I’m compiling it now to catch any COBOL syntax issues and then I’ll run the binary to verify the counts against the full game tree.

The standalone GnuCOBOL program is in [game15.cob](/Users/mathieuacher/SANDBOX/game15-cobol-codex/game15.cob). It enumerates every legal completed game with explicit backtracking, stops each branch at the first win, and counts Player 1 wins, Player 2 wins, draws, and total completed games.

I compiled it with `cobc -x -free game15.cob` and ran `./game15`. The program reports:

- Player 1 wins: `131,184`
- Player 2 wins: `77,904`
- Draws: `46,080`
- Total games: `255,168`
I’m turning the workspace into a Git repository now, and I’ll add a minimal `.gitignore` so the compiled binary stays out of the first commit.
The only file edit is `.gitignore`. Next I’m initializing the repo on a `codex/` branch, staging the source files, and creating the initial commit.
The commit succeeded. I’m doing one quick status check to confirm the tree is clean and the build artifact is being ignored as intended.

The last run exposed a regression: the rebuilt binary is still showing the old pool output. I’m checking the source around `DISPLAY-RULES` and fixing whatever the compiler actually saw.

Added [gameN.cob](/Users/mathieuacher/SANDBOX/game15-cobol-codex/gameN.cob). It accepts `./gameN <target-sum> [<max-number>]`, validates the inputs, chooses a default `max-number` of `target-sum - 3` when omitted (minimum `3`, capped at `999`), prints the rules, pool range, full number pool, and all winning triples, and exhaustively counts games when `max-number <= 9`.

I rebuilt it with `cobc -x -free gameN.cob -o /tmp/gameN` and verified:
- `/tmp/gameN 15 9` reports the expected 8 winning triples and the standard counts: P1 `131,184`, P2 `77,904`, draws `46,080`, total `255,168`.

- `/tmp/gameN` shows the usage message.
- Large target sums such as `/tmp/gameN 123456789 9` are handled correctly.
